proposal.blind_spot: All kernels look identically 'DRAM-bound with coalesced loads', so the optimizer cannot tell whether the real ceiling is the L1/LSU transaction path or DRAM itself, and cannot see whether the equally large write stream is sector-efficient.

rationale.l1tex__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustai: HIGH -> L1/LSU pipe is saturated: vectorize to 128-bit accesses, widen tiles, drop sector-splitting masked accesses / LOW -> wall is downstream: cut bytes via fusion, smaller dtype, removing read-modify-write round trips, or accept roofline and do not churn the kernel
rationale.smsp__sass_average_data_bytes_per_sector: HIGH -> stores are well coalesced, leave the store path alone and attack traffic volume or loads / LOW -> write traffic is amplified by partial sectors: stage outputs in shared memory and write contiguously, or remap grid so warps own contiguous output ranges

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:A cut at ~93% of peak sustained DRAM throughput corresponds to the real physical regime of memory-bandwidth saturation (memory-bound vs not), which generalizes across kernels, whereas an absolute byte count is workload-size-dependent and a 9.4% SM-throughput cut marks no meaningful hardware boundary.
